svg.text: The spindle is adjustable — but it is not a position dial
Fusimotor drive can preserve spindle sensitivity and bias afferent responses, but it does not specify one desired muscle length.
The same spindle under three conditions
Active shortening can unload the parallel spindle unless fusimotor drive and external mechanics maintain tension.
Distinct intrafusal fibers and sensory endings
Fusimotor state changes the response to the same stretch
Reference-configuration models describe a loop, not an anatomical dial

g.text: Relaxed muscle in this schematic; external lengthening loads the spindle.
external stretch tensions the sensory region

text.tspan: Ia responds briskly during length change;
II emphasizes the sustained change in length.

g.text: 2. Active shortening with little fusimotor support
The surrounding muscle shortens faster than the spindle is retensioned.

text.tspan: Sensitivity is reduced until tension is restored;
complete silence is possible but not obligatory.

g.text: Coordinated activity need not be fixed, proportional, or spike-for-spike.

text.tspan: Afferent responsiveness is preserved, but Ia and II output
depends on the mixture of dynamic and static fusimotor drive.

svg.text: All firing patterns are schematic. “Coactivation” means coordinated control, not a hard-wired one-to-one coupling.

text.tspan: Ia and II both transduce intrafusal deformation, but they sample different fibers and regions.
Dynamic and static gamma targeting is strongly biased rather than perfectly exclusive.
Schematic complement: intrafusal fiber number and mixture vary among spindles.
Neither sensory ending subtracts actual length from a stored desired length.

g.text: Illustrative normalized responses — not recorded data. Dynamic and static drive bias response properties; they are not pure velocity and position channels.
SERVO / REFERENCE-CONFIGURATION HYPOTHESIS — not an identified anatomical circuit
Gamma drive is one adjustable component — not the desired-length command. No single spindle reports a clean error signal.

svg.text: Gamma activity does more than prevent slack: it changes how spindle afferents respond, with the pattern adjusted to the task rather than rigidly coupled to alpha drive.
